# Direct runtime dependencies. The production image installs from
# requirements.lock.txt (hash-pinned, generated by `uv export` — see below);
# this file is the human-edited manifest. Keep it in sync with
# [project.dependencies] in pyproject.toml, then run:
#   uv lock && uv export --format requirements-txt -o requirements.lock.txt
APScheduler==3.11.2
# Brotli decoder: the shared HTTP session advertises Accept-Encoding derived
# from what urllib3 can decode; installing brotli turns "br" support on
# (nadoexplorer's edge serves brotli-compressed JSON — 2026-07-14 incident).
Brotli==1.2.0
# >=50.0.0 clears CVE-2026-69248 and CVE-2026-69249 (both fixed in 49.0.0) plus
# CVE-2026-69247 (PKCS#7 Bleichenbacher oracle, fixed only in 50.0.0) — so 50.0.0
# is the floor that clears all three. Fernet token format is unchanged, so
# linked-signer keys encrypted under 48.x still decrypt (core/crypto.py).
cryptography==50.0.0
eth-account>=0.8.0,<0.9.0
# Native libsecp256k1 signing backend for eth-keys (the ECDSA under eth-account).
# WITHOUT this, eth-keys uses its pure-Python backend (eth_keys.backends.native),
# ~15-25x slower AND GIL-bound for the entire signature — so a strategy's order-
# signing burst pins the one GIL and starves the single event loop, which is why
# more CPU didn't fix tap latency (one process, one GIL). coincurve (libsecp256k1)
# is ~20x faster and RELEASES the GIL during the C sign, so the loop stays
# responsive and the 2nd vCPU is actually used. eth-keys auto-selects
# CoinCurveECCBackend whenever coincurve is importable — no code change needed.
coincurve>=21,<22
# Direct dependency (lowiq_relay_client, hl_client); also pulled in by openai.
httpx>=0.27,<1.0
nado-protocol==0.3.3
openai==2.17.0
Pillow>=10.4.0
pinecone>=8.1,<9.0
psycopg2-binary==2.9.11
python-dotenv==1.2.2
python-telegram-bot[webhooks]==22.6
requests==2.33.0
websockets>=10.0.0,<14.0.0
